title: Career Roadmap: Aerospace Technician
summary: An Aerospace Technician supports the manufacturing, inspection, assembly, testing, maintenance, or repair of aircraft, spacecraft, engines, and aerospace components.

facts.Current degree: Aviation & Aerospace Programmes – Aerospace Manufacturing / MRO

about.label: Recommended Education
about.text: B.Tech/B.E. in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, or Manufacturing Engineering; relevant diploma pathways may also be suitable

about.label: Primary Industries
about.text: Aerospace manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, component production, and aerospace testing

about.label: Workplaces
about.text: Aircraft and engine manufacturers, MRO facilities, component suppliers, aerospace production plants, and testing laboratories

about.label: Career Type
about.text: Technical Operations, Manufacturing, Inspection, Testing, Maintenance Support

blocks.label: Important career note
blocks.text: Aerospace Technician is a broad occupational title. Some positions focus on aircraft structures and mechanical systems, while others involve engines, electrical systems, avionics, composite materials, or manufacturing equipment. An engineering degree can support technical and supervisory pathways, but hands-on technician jobs may require a relevant diploma, practical training, and employer-specific competency assessments. Licensed aircraft maintenance work requires the applicable regulatory qualifications and authorisations.
An Aerospace Technician supports the manufacturing, inspection, assembly, testing, maintenance, or repair of aircraft, spacecraft, engines, and aerospace components.

The role combines practical technical ability with precision, documentation, quality control, and safety discipline. Technicians work from engineering drawings, work instructions, technical manuals, inspection criteria, and approved procedures.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Assemble and inspect aerospace components and subassemblies.
Read engineering drawings, technical specifications, and work instructions.
Use measuring instruments and appropriate workshop tools.
Support manufacturing, machining, fabrication, and composite-material processes.
Assist with functional tests and equipment checks.
Identify defects and report deviations from specifications.
Maintain traceability of parts, materials, and inspection records.
Follow quality-management, occupational-safety, and foreign-object-debris prevention practices.
Support troubleshooting and corrective actions under the relevant level of authorisation.
Coordinate with engineers, quality inspectors, production teams, and maintenance personnel.

blocks.text: The precise responsibilities depend on the employer, product, and specialisation. Technicians must not certify aircraft maintenance or release products to service unless they hold the required authorisation.

blocks.text: These stages are illustrative. Progress depends on the qualification pathway, practical experience, employer requirements, and any applicable licences or authorisations.
The following plan assumes a four-year engineering degree. Students enrolled in three-year or diploma programmes should adapt the stages to their course structure.
Year 1 — Engineering Foundations
Subjects to learn
Practical activities

items.text: Learn safe workshop practices and measurement techniques.
Use vernier calipers, micrometers, and other basic measuring instruments.
Create simple CAD models of mechanical components.
Learn technical documentation and spreadsheet basics.

Subjects to learn

Document measurements and compare them with sample specifications.

blocks.label: Regulatory distinction
blocks.text: In India, aircraft maintenance licensing and certification requirements are separate from a general aerospace or mechanical engineering degree. Candidates intending to perform licensed aircraft maintenance should verify the current Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) requirements and the employer's approved procedures.

blocks.text: Use training components and fictional or public data. Do not perform experimental modifications to aircraft, engines, or safety-critical components outside an authorised facility.
Use this five-point scale:

items.text: 3/5: Can complete academic or supervised tasks with guidance
4/5: Can perform independently within a trained and authorised role
5/5: Can lead, coach, and improve technical processes

blocks.text: These are development targets, not formal licensing or competency standards.
Relevant practical experience is particularly important because employers need evidence that candidates can work safely, accurately, and consistently.

blocks.text: Recommended progression

items.text: Choose a technical specialisation by the second or third year.
Learn the CAD, measurement, or testing tools relevant to that pathway.
Apply for supervised manufacturing, quality, testing, or MRO internships.
Maintain a portfolio of drawings, inspection reports, test analyses, and projects.
Learn the employer's quality system and documentation expectations.
Complete any additional training or certification required for the target role.
Apply for suitable entry-level technical positions.

Postgraduate study is optional for many technician roles. It may help candidates move into engineering, research, manufacturing leadership, or advanced technical functions.

blocks.text: Adoption varies across manufacturers and programmes. Technicians should build strong fundamentals before specialising in emerging technologies.
A strong Aerospace Technician candidate should combine:

blocks.label: Engineering fundamentals
blocks.text: Materials, mechanics, drawings, and tolerances.

blocks.label: Practical technical skills
blocks.text: Measurement, assembly, manufacturing, or testing.

blocks.label: Quality and safety
blocks.text: Inspection, traceability, documentation, and safe work practices.

blocks.label: Digital capability
blocks.text: CAD, spreadsheets, production systems, and relevant technical software.

blocks.label: Troubleshooting
blocks.text: Structured problem-solving and evidence-based defect analysis.

blocks.label: Specialisation
blocks.text: One strong pathway such as structures, manufacturing, engines, avionics, or testing.

blocks.label: Professional readiness
blocks.text: Relevant practical training, internships, and any required qualifications or authorisations.
By graduation, the student should aim to have:

items.text: A relevant engineering or technical qualification.
Strong engineering drawing and measurement skills.
Practical exposure to manufacturing, inspection, testing, or maintenance support.
Working knowledge of quality assurance and technical documentation.
Proficiency in at least one relevant CAD, testing, or data-analysis tool.
Internship or workshop experience supported by verifiable project evidence.
A portfolio containing technical drawings, inspection reports, test analyses, or process plans.
A clear understanding of any additional qualification or authorisation needed for the chosen role.

items: specialisation in aerospace production, inspection, testing, or MRO
senior technician, specialist, or technical supervisor

blocks.text: The most employable candidates combine precision, hands-on capability, safety discipline, technical documentation, and a strong understanding of quality requirements. Choose the specialisation early, because an aerospace manufacturing technician, an avionics technician, and a licensed aircraft maintenance professional may follow different training and authorisation pathways.
